key: And Samuel said to Saul: ‘Thou hast done foolishly; thou hast not kept the commandment of the LORD thy God, which He commanded thee; for now would the LORD have established thy kingdom upon Israel for ever.
s: Finding that Saul has offered the burnt-offering without him, Samuel rebukes the king; Radak, on 13:13, reads the folly as lost trust in God: doubting the prophet would come in time, Saul thought neither he nor Israel could be saved by waiting longer.

evidence.gloss: And now, because you did not believe that I would come at my time, you denied me and my prophecy and did not keep the commandment of the LORD your God which He commanded you through me; I told you to wait for me to offer the burnt-offerings, and when you did not, and were afraid, as you say, you rebelled against the word of the LORD and removed trust in Him from your heart, for you thought that you and Israel would not be saved if you waited longer.
